attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated as his assessment rather than quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: This is an unhedged present-tense observation with three parts. The normalised text drops 'LLM' before 'profits', which slightly widens it. The claim's target and the contract both keep the LLM scope, so this is acceptable.

contract.note: These are plain, ordinary readings: commodity means substantial substitution and price competition, 'hard to find' means uncommon, and 'billions every month' means at least $2B a month. Using Q3 2025, the latest quarter before the post, is a reasonable window. None of these readings is stretched for or against Marcus.

evidence.note: A dated press estimate for the target quarter: The Register infers a quarterly OpenAI loss of more than $12B (over $4B a month) from Microsoft's equity-method loss and stake. It is clearly an estimate, not an OpenAI filing, but the contract allows a credible estimate above $6B a quarter to support the financial part.

DeepSeek's own announcement of a 50%+ API price cut in the target quarter. This fits price competition, but one supplier's cut, which it attributes to efficiency gains, does not show market-wide substitution.

NIST/CAISI's evaluation found DeepSeek models lag the best U.S. models. That shows some differentiation, but under the contract one differentiated model does not refute commoditization, and it says nothing about profits.

reviews.rationale: Of the three parts, only the OpenAI loss is supported: a credible press estimate (e1) puts the Q3 2025 loss above $12B, over $4B a month. The commodity part has only context: one supplier's price cut and an evaluation showing capability gaps. There is no evidence on LLM profits outside Nvidia. Nothing in the packet contradicts any part, but two of the three parts are unsettled, so the claim as a whole is unresolved.
